key_insight: CoorDex shows that humanoids do not need to stop walking to manipulate objects: body motion and dexterous hand control can be coordinated continuously through a learned latent residual policy. This enables more natural, high-DoF loco-manipulation than simple open-close grasping.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the common limitation in humanoid robotics where locomotion and manipulation are treated as separate phases, forcing robots to stop before interacting with objects. It also tackles the difficulty of controlling high-DoF hands and body motions together in real time.
method: Learn a coordinated latent residual control pipeline that maps high-dimensional body and hand commands into a compact action space.
Use simulated training to learn continuous dexterous loco-manipulation instead of stop-and-go behavior.
Combine body and dexterous hand priors so the humanoid can manipulate objects while maintaining movement.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a practical path toward more capable embodied agents that can operate fluidly in dynamic environments. It may improve robotics systems that need simultaneous mobility and manipulation, such as service robots, assistive robots, and warehouse humanoids.
